transcript: I'm a romance novel girly, and I entirely credit it to my middle school obsession with Jane Austen. I've read every book, I've seen every adaptation, and this week, I got to live my best Jane Austen life while celebrating the release of the new sense, sensibility movie. First, I went to terrain at the Brooklyn Botanical Garden for a dreamy afternoon with lemonade, lots of incredible snacks, and a poet who wrote us each our own home. I literally almost cried reading this. Train is truly the most beautiful store I have ever stepped foot in. And then we got to take a planter workshop, and apparently I'm a gardener now. Friend Morgan and I had little really the best time. We got to put our hands in the dirt, and we got a bunch of different plants, and we had to figure out where they looked best. And it was just really nice to be doing, like, a craft with my hands. Although my favourite part was actually the moss. I loved figuring out, like, where all the moss would go. But yes, sipping lemonade and surrounded by flowers, I truly have never felt more like Jane Austen in my entire life. it was time to see an early screening of sense and sensibility. It was actually a Pajama Party screening, which is how all movies should be experienced. We got to build our own little bouquet, Hayes, load up on snacks, and then we got These cutie little goodie bags with a claw clip and some lip balm and an eye mask. All of the sleepover party essentials. And right before the movie was about to start, they surprised us when Daisy Edgar Jones and Esme Creed Miles, the Dashwood sisters themselves, walked in. So proud of this film. So excited to share it with you. Get lost in the romance. Um. I'm so excited for you to spend two hours with the dashwoods. Thank you so much. And then it was time for the movie. Oh, my god. Why am I crying? I'm not. Well, it was a perfect adaptation. The yearning, exquisite longing glances off the charts. I ate up every single second. You can't miss seeing sense and sensibility in theaters October 16th.
classificationReason: A lifestyle/events vlog about a Jane Austen-themed celebration and an early film screening of Sense and Sensibility. No Broadway/West End stage production is reviewed.
